lines.text: Some claims need a human. Chain the human to the proof.
An agent wants to deploy to production. No approval in the chain — the claim halts. Evidence missing. The gate doesn't guess, and it doesn't forget.
The approval lands where humans live: who is asking, what claim, which role must sign. No hallway approvals.
A senior engineer reviews. Approves. The signature is real, scoped, and expiring.
And the approval chains into the signed envelope — the human is now part of the proof.
Admit. The deploy proceeds — with a name attached.
